blocks.heading: WELCOME — DAY 1
blocks.board_text:
Student Mode · Day 1 of 5

Today's focus:
• What cloud computing actually is
• Why companies moved to cloud
• Regions, the AWS console, and scaling

How this class works:
• I teach on the board while I speak
• After each step, I ask a quick check — answer on your mic
• At the end: summary + doubt session
blocks.ren_voice: Welcome. Naan Ren. Ithu Student Mode Day 1. IAM, VPC, console tickets ellam apram. First cloud-a clear-a understand pannanum — enna, yen win aaguchu, AWS eppadi organize aaguchu. Step by step poguvom. Naan board-la ezhuthi teach panren. Oru idea mudinchaa, short question kekkuven — mic-la answer pannunga. Ready-aa? Foundation-la start panrom.

blocks.heading: WHAT IS CLOUD COMPUTING?
blocks.board_text:
Cloud computing = using the internet to access computers, storage, and software owned and maintained by someone else.

Instead of buying a server and storing it in your office, you rent one from a provider over the internet.

Three major providers:
• AWS (Amazon Web Services) — largest, ~31% market share
• Google Cloud
• Microsoft Azure

You pay only for what you use.
You can scale up or down instantly.
You never touch a physical machine.
blocks.ren_voice: Cloud computing-nu solnaa, internet-la irukkura computers, storage, software — ellathaiyum veyra yaaravadhu own panni manage panna — rent panni use panrathum maathiri. Namba sonthamaaga server vangitu office-la vachirukkathukku pathilamaaga, internet-la AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure kitta rent pannuvom. Electricity generator vaangala — grid-la connect panni use panrom, month-la bill katrom. Cloud-um same maathiri. AWS ellam ulleye periya data centers-la servers vachirukkanga. Namba account eduthu, use panna, month-la pay pannuvom. Oru physical machine thodalavae thodalai.

check_question.question: Before we move on — in your own words, what is the one thing that makes cloud computing different from a company buying its own servers?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Exactly — rent panrom, vangala. Andha oru difference ellathayum maathiruchu: upfront capital illai, hardware maintain panna vendam, use pannrathuku mattum pay pannuvom. Adhu-taan cloud computing-oda foundation.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: 'Rent' versus 'buy'-nu yosinga. Server vanganaa, nambathu — upfront pay panrom, maintain pannuvom, use aagadhappo kuda full cost pay pannuvom. Cloud-la, veyra yaarodhu computer-a rent panni use pannuvom, use pannrathukku mattum pay pannuvom. Own to rent-ku shift — adhu core idea.

blocks.heading: WHY DO COMPANIES USE CLOUD?
blocks.board_text:
Before cloud computing:
• Buy servers upfront (crores of rupees, weeks to procure)
• Rent a data center rack (long-term lease)
• Hire staff to maintain the hardware
• Guess how many servers you will need (usually wrong)
• Pay full cost even during low-traffic periods

With cloud computing:
• No upfront hardware cost — start from zero
• Scale to 10x capacity in minutes, not months
• Pay only for what you use — idle resources cost nothing
• No physical maintenance — the cloud provider handles hardware failures
blocks.ren_voice: Cloud varathukku munnaadi, oru startup product launch panna server vanganum, data center-la rack rent pannanum, hardware maintain panna aalunga vekkanum, ellam serndhaa months of work, crores of rupees — apprama product-ku oru line code ezhutha illai. Guess problem kooda irundhuchu: six months-la how many servers venum-nu decide pannanum. Kammiya vanganaa, traffic spike-la site pochu. Athigama vanganaa, idle-a full cost pay panrom. Cloud rendu-um solve pannuchu. Zero-la irundhu start pannuvom, double overnight aanaalum minutes-la scale panna mudiyum. Traffic kurayum pothu scale back pannuvom. Idle capacity-ku oru paisa-um pay pannaatheenga.

check_question.question: If a startup's product suddenly becomes viral and traffic goes 20x overnight — what happens with physical servers versus cloud?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Exactly right — physical servers-la, crash aaguchu, new hardware weeks kazhichu varum. Cloud-la, minutes-la scale up panna mudiyum, traffic handle panna mudiyum. Adhu technical advantage mattum illai — business survival advantage.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: Timeline-a yosinga. Physical servers-la new hardware order pannanum, delivery wait pannanum, setup pannanum — weeks. Appova namba users down site-a hit pannikittu irukkanga. Cloud-la, minutes-la more capacity appear aaguchu. Viral moment-a handle panna maathaara startup survive aaguchu. Hardware-a wait panna maathaara survive aagathu.

blocks.heading: HOW CLOUD COMPUTING WORKS — THE MENTAL MODEL
blocks.board_text:
AWS has data centers in cities around the world. Each city cluster = a Region.

Mumbai = ap-south-1
Singapore = ap-southeast-1
Virginia (US) = us-east-1

Inside a Region, you create Resources — the things you actually use:
• Virtual computer → EC2
• File storage → S3
• Database → RDS

You access everything through the AWS Management Console — a website.
Resources start in seconds. AWS bills you by the hour or by the byte.
blocks.ren_voice: Eppadi actual-a work pannum-nu solren. AWS, world-la cities-la periya data centers vachirukkanga. Oru geographic location-a Region-nu solvaanga. Mumbai-a ap-south-1-nu AWS solluchu. 'ap' Asia Pacific, 'south' South Asia, '1' first region there. Singapore ap-southeast-1. Virginia us-east-1. Resources create pannaa, which Region-la irukkanum-nu choose pannuvom. Oru Region-ku ulleye actual things create pannuvom. Virtual computer-a EC2-nu solvaanga. File storage-a S3. Managed database-a RDS. Ellam AWS Management Console-la — oru website-la — access pannuvom. Login pannuvaanga, service-ku navigate pannuvaanga, configure pannuvaanga, seconds-la start aaguchu. Month-end-la use pannrathukku bill pay pannuvom. Adhu-taan complete loop.

check_question.question: If FoodQuick wants its servers to be physically close to customers in Mumbai — which AWS Region would you deploy in?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Correct — ap-south-1, Mumbai region. Users-ku physical-a close-a irundha latency kammiyaaguchu — user-oda phone-la irundhu server-ku request travel panna time kammiyaaguchu. Right Region choose pannradhu, AWS-la deploy panna first decisions-la oru.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: Mumbai Region in AWS, ap-south-1-nu solvaanga. 'ap' Asia Pacific, 'south' South Asia, '1' first region. ap-south-1-la deploy pannaa, physical servers Mumbai-la — India-la irukkura users-ku lowest possible latency, geographically close servers-la irundhu.

blocks.heading: WHAT THE AWS CONSOLE LOOKS LIKE
blocks.board_text:
When you log into AWS:

→ Top navigation bar: Services menu, search bar, Region selector, account name
→ Services menu: grouped by category — Compute, Storage, Database, Networking, Security
→ Region selector (top right): dropdown showing which Region you are currently working in
→ Search bar: type any service name (EC2, S3, IAM) — it appears immediately
→ Home screen: recently visited services, cost overview, news

The Region selector is critical — every resource you create lives in the Region you have selected.
Creating something in ap-south-1 is not visible when you switch to us-east-1.
blocks.ren_voice: AWS Management Console first open pannaa enna paappeenga-nu solren. Top-la navigation bar irukkum. Left-la Services menu — click pannaa every AWS service grouped-a paappeenga: Compute, Storage, Database, Networking, Security. Middle-la search bar — EC2-nu type pannaa immediately appear aaguchu. Right side-la Region selector — currently which Region-la work pannrom-nu show pannum dropdown. Ithu oru most important things-la oru — watch pannanum. Create panna every resource, select panna Region-la-taan irukkum. Mumbai-la EC2 server create panni, Region selector-a Virginia-ku switch pannaa, andha server poitadhu maathiri thonum — illai, different Region-la irukkum. New engineers ithula romba confuse aaguvaanga. Always Region selector-a check pannu, yedhaavadhu panna munnaadi.

check_question.question: You create an EC2 server in the Mumbai region, then someone tells you it is missing. What is the first thing you check?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Exactly — Region selector. Server almost certainly irukkum, veyra Region-la paakkiromlanu visible aagathu. AWS-la new engineers-ku ithuthan single most common confusion. Region first check pannradhu, neraya time waste save panna.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: Answer: top right console-la Region selector. yaravadhu ap-south-1 (Mumbai)-la server create pannanga, namba us-east-1 (Virginia)-la current-a paakaranaa, server invisible — different Region-la irukkum. Region selector Mumbai-ku switch pannaa appear aaguchu. Yedhaavadhu missing-nu conclude panna munnaadi, always Region check pannu.

blocks.heading: YOUR TURN — WHAT WOULD YOU DO?
blocks.board_text:
Scenario:
A friend is starting a small food delivery business in Chennai.
They need:
• A website for customers to order food
• A place to store restaurant photos and menus
• A database to track orders

They ask you: 'Should we rent a server at a local data center for ₹50,000/month, or use AWS?'

What do you tell them, and why?
blocks.ren_voice: Oru friend Chennai-la food delivery business start panraanga. Customer orders-ku website, restaurant photos store panna idham, orders track panna database — ellam venum. Local data center-la fixed ₹50,000/month server rent panraanaa, illa AWS use panraanaa-nu ninga kitta kekkuvaanga. Beginning-la how much traffic varum-nu theriyaadhu. Fast grow aagalaam, slow grow aagalaam. Enna solluveengaa?

check_question.question: Walk me through your recommendation — AWS or the local server, and what are the two strongest reasons for your choice?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Good reasoning — AWS correct call. Two most important reasons: first, avanga traffic-a theriyaadhu still, ₹50,000 flat-a pay panna, use aagaadha capacity-ku waste. AWS-la actual usage-ku mattum pay pannuvom. Second, suddenly popular aanaalum — minutes-la scale panna mudiyum. Local fixed server, unexpected load-la crash aaguchu, fast path to more capacity illai.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: New business-ku rendu specific risks yosinga. First: beginning-la almost yarum use panna illaadhappo? ₹50,000/month, 5% capacity-la run aagura server — neraya wasted money. AWS actual usage-ku charge pannum. Second: suddenly really popular aanaalum? Fixed local server, quickly scale panna way illai. AWS, minutes-la 10x traffic handle panna mudiyum. Early-stage, unpredictable demand-ku cloud default correct.

blocks.heading: WHAT HAPPENS WHEN YOU IGNORE CLOUD
blocks.board_text:
A real mistake — 2011, Friendster vs Facebook:

• Friendster (peak: 115 million users) owned physical servers in data centers
• Facebook moved to cloud infrastructure early
• Friendster's traffic surged — they could not scale their physical servers fast enough
• Page load time: 40 seconds. Users left.
• Facebook scaled with traffic using cloud-like infrastructure — page loads stayed fast

Friendster was the larger, more established platform.
Facebook won because it could scale. Friendster could not.

Today: every serious tech company runs on cloud. Physical server ownership for web applications is largely obsolete.
blocks.ren_voice: Scale panna mudiyaadhappo enna aaguchu-nu oru real story solren. Friendster — Facebook varathukku munnaadiyaana dominant social network. Peak-la 115 million users. Aana Friendster physical servers own pannuchu. Traffic, hardware procure and install panna maadhaara fast-a grow aanaa, page load times 40 seconds hit aanuchu. Users 40 seconds wait panna maataanga. Pogutaanga. Facebook smaller irundha, aana demand-oda scale panna infrastructure build panna pannuchu. Page loads fast-a irundhuchu. Users irundhanga. Friendster 115 million users-la irundhu irrelevance-ku ponaa, few years-la. Physical infrastructure, scale panna mudiyaadhappo, companies-a end panna pannuchu. Cloud infrastructure, minutes-la scale panna, companies-a enable panna pannuchu. Theoretical concern illai — documented pattern, repeatedly play out aaguchu.

check_question.question: In the Friendster story, the core technical failure was not their product — it was something else. What was it?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Exactly — scale panna mudiyaadhaa infrastructure. Product-ku users irundhanga. Demand irundhuchu. Aana physical servers load handle panna mudiyaadhaa, new servers fast enough add panna mudiyaadhaa. Infrastructure failure. Cloud computing specifically ithai solve panna design panna — minutes-la capacity add panna mudiyum, weeks illai.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: Product problem illai — Friendster-ku 115 million users use panna venum-nu irundhanga. Problem physical servers load handle panna mudiyaadhaa, new physical servers add panna too long aachu. Infrastructure failure. Cloud computing specifically ithai solve panna — minutes-la capacity add panna mudiyum, weeks illai.

blocks.heading: QUICK CHALLENGE
blocks.board_text:
A company runs 10 EC2 servers to handle their normal daily traffic.
On New Year's Eve, they expect 50x the normal traffic for about 4 hours.

What should they do before midnight?
And what should they do after 4am when traffic returns to normal?

Think about what cloud makes possible that physical servers cannot.
blocks.ren_voice: Oru company normally 10 EC2 servers run panruvaanga. Innikku New Year's Eve. Midnight-la irundhu roughly 4 hours, 50 times normal traffic expect panraanga. Midnight-ku munnaadi enna panna vendiyathu, 4am-la traffic normal-ku thirumba aanaa enna panna vendiyathu? Cloud actually enna possible pannuchu-nu yosinga.

check_question.question: What are your two actions — one before midnight, one after 4am?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Right — midnight munnaadi, scale up. 50x traffic handle panna enough additional EC2 servers launch pannunga, 10-la 100-ku or more. 4am-la traffic normal-ku thirumba aanaa, scale back down pannunga. Extra servers terminate pannu, pay stop aaguchu. Andha extra 90 servers-ku roughly 4 hours pay pannuvom, permanently illai. Adhu-taan cloud enable panradhu — temporary capacity with temporary cost.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: Rendu moves: midnight munnaadi, scale up — more EC2 instances launch pannunga, 50x traffic handle panna. Cloud, 10 servers-la 100 servers-ku minutes-la ponga allow panrum. 4am-la scale back down — extra servers terminate, pay stop. Few hours extra capacity-ku mattum pay pannuvom. Physical servers-a own panna company, peak 4 hours-ku year-round 100 servers own panni pay pannanum. Cloud that waste eliminate panniduchu.

blocks.heading: HOW ZEPTO USED CLOUD TO SCALE
blocks.board_text:
Zepto — Indian 10-minute grocery delivery:

• Launched in 2021 with a small engineering team
• Reached 10 million+ users within 18 months of launch
• Could not have scaled that fast with physical server procurement
• Used AWS to spin up new compute capacity as demand grew — in hours, not months
• Scaled back during off-peak hours to avoid paying for idle capacity
• Today: one of India's fastest-growing consumer tech companies

Physical infrastructure timeline: 6–12 weeks to procure, install, and configure servers
AWS timeline: minutes

For a startup moving at Zepto's speed, cloud was not a preference — it was the only viable option.
blocks.ren_voice: Ninga therinja oru company-la close pannuvom. Zepto 2021-la launch aanaa — 10-minute grocery delivery. 18 months-la India-la millions of users-ku serve pannivaanga. Eppadi ithanai speed-la infrastructure build panna mudiyum, how big you will get, how fast — theriyaadhappo? Physical servers-a ithai panna mudiyaadhu. Procurement timeline alone — 6 to 12 weeks, order, deliver, install, configure — means namba always actual demand-ku behind-a irukkuvom. Zepto actually enna panna pannanga: AWS use panna. Demand grow aanappo, more compute capacity turn on pannanga — EC2 instances, hours-la. Raathiri 3am-la quiet period-la scale back panna, pay stop pannaanga. Infrastructure cost, actual revenue-a track panna pannuchu, upfront hardware bet illai. Startup speed-la, oru year-la 10x growth possible-a irukkura market-la, cloud preference illai. Scale panna maathaara only architecture.

lesson_summary.board_text:
What you must know after Day 1:

• Cloud computing = renting compute, storage, and networking over the internet — no hardware to buy
• AWS is the largest cloud provider — it owns the servers, you create resources and pay for usage
• Regions = AWS data centers in specific cities. Mumbai = ap-south-1.
• Resources start in seconds. Billing starts when they run, stops when you shut them down.
• Scale up for traffic spikes, scale down when quiet — you never pay for idle capacity
• The Region selector in the AWS console controls everything — always check it first
lesson_summary.ren_voice: Day 1-la enna eduthukitta-nu solren. Cloud computing infrastructure rent pannradhu — physical machine thodalavae thodalai. AWS-taan most infrastructure irukkum, Regions-a organize panna — India users-ku closest, ap-south-1 Mumbai-la. Console-la resources create pannuvom, seconds-la start aaguchu, use pannrathukku pay pannuvom, done aanalaa stop aaguchu. Traffic spike-ku scale up, quiet-a irundha scale down. Idle capacity-ku pay pannaatheenga. Console-la Region selector — always check pannu, yedhaavadhu panna munnaadi. Naalaikku, andha cloud account-a yaaru access panna mudiyum, enna panna mudiyum-nu deeper poga — adhu IAM, ellathukum foundation.
